attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.50.0/24 on eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.60.0/24 on eth2), fixed a default-route asymmetry on node2/node3 with explicit static routes via node1, opened node3's host firewalld for TCP/5432 from lan-a, and applied a default-drop VyOS forward filter with an established/related accept and a specific accept for TCP/5432 from eth1→eth2. Verified node2 can reach node3:5432 while all other traffic (other TCP ports, ICMP, and reverse-direction lan-b→lan-a) is rejected in both directions. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (native reboot mechanisms), boot_id changes proved real restarts, and full policy/connectivity was re-verified as recovered after each restart.
